reason: The only offered combination adds the filaments needed for the fibre to pull.
expectation: I expect organized actin and myosin filaments inside the fibre, though a calcium signal may still be needed to activate pulling.

reaction: The covered sites make the need for an activation signal clear.
reason: The only offered combination supplies the calcium signal needed to activate the filaments.
expectation: I expect calcium to uncover actin's grip sites so myosin can attach and pull.

effect: Calcium exposes the grip sites, allowing ATP-dependent cycling and filament sliding; the filaments themselves do not shorten.
reaction: The distinction between fibre shortening and filament shortening is useful.
reason: The only offered combination should return calcium to storage so the fibre can become ready again.
expectation: I expect ATP-powered pumps to remove calcium from around the filaments, allowing the grip sites to be covered again.

effect: ATP-powered calcium storage stops pulling, and an outside pull lengthens the fibre; the goal now shifts to building and attaching muscles.
reaction: It is useful to see that relaxation requires ATP and that lengthening needs an outside pull.
reason: The only offered combination adds extracellular matrix, apparently a step toward assembling muscle tissue.

reaction: The distinction between the fibre membrane and surrounding connective layer is helpful.
reason: Both muscles are needed; I’ll assemble the biceps first.

reaction: The contrasting attachment positions clearly explain how similar muscle pulls produce opposite movements.

mostWorthwhile.text: The calcium-triggered sliding cycle was most worthwhile: the planned sequence connects ATP use to pulling and distinguishes fibre shortening from filament shortening.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps repeated the biceps assembly and force-path inset, making that passage less engaging.

surprise.text: Relaxation also requires ATP to pump calcium back into storage, while an outside pull lengthens the fibre.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though choosing which muscle to assemble or attach first was an arbitrary ordering choice; both were needed.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the assembled arm works in a broader system; the connection between muscle attachments and opposite movements was interesting.
